Alaska.Ai — The Stack Draft

2026-06-07 · branch claude/linkedin-stack-2026-06-07-02
No defensible target this cycle — no post generated

Why this cycle produced no post

The 14-day window (May 24–June 7, 2026) produced zero survivors. The window was broadened to 21 days (May 17–June 7, 2026) per protocol. The broadened window also produced zero survivors. Every serious candidate failed at least one gate as follows. C_V1 (BEAD Subgrant Execution Stack): Gate 1 FAIL — the two confirmed in-window news articles (KUCB May 27, Alaska Public Media June 1) cover GCI's Aleutian cable outage and satellite backup service; neither article mentions BEAD, the Alaska Broadband Office, Thomas Lochner, or subgrantee grant agreements. The connection is inferential, not direct implication. Gate 3 additional FAIL — Layer 2 (NIST Notice of Award Amendment) controlling actor is unnamed in any fetchable primary source; Thomas Lochner as ABO Director appears only via an email address in an image-heavy PDF, not in a statute, org chart, or agency page that formally designates him as director; Layer 5 (THPO veto authority) is not documented in the ABO agency page that was successfully fetched. C_CS2 (Doyon CEO Transition Stack): Gate 1 FAIL on two counts — the Doyon CEO announcement was published March 9, 2026 (90 days outside the broadened window), and the source is a corporate newsroom page, not an independent news outlet. No independent news outlet covered the Winkelman appointment or the Doyon fiber project in the May 17–June 7 window. The Doyon April 2026 project update confirms the ADNR river easement was already granted in late summer 2025, removing the BLM/ADNR layer as a live decision point. Gate 5 additional FAIL — Winkelman's individual binary authority (vs. board vote) to authorize the July 2026 Yukon River cable-laying is not documented in any fetchable primary source. C_R1 (NRC Part 57 Microreactor Licensing Stack): Gate 1 FAIL — the primary trigger (POWER Magazine April 27, 2026) is 41 days before June 7, outside even the 21-day broadened window. The June 5 Antares Mark-0 criticality article is in-window but does not mention Alaska, Eielson AFB, or NRC Part 57. Gate 3 additional FAIL — the Orrick LLP analysis URL (L2 primary source) returns 404; the NRC OAR agency page returns 404; the Alaska DEC siting permit page does not name a specific controlling official. Gate 5 additional FAIL — Alaska DEC Layer (L4) does not name a specific official for the siting permit decision. C_F1 (Quintillion Nome-Homer Express): Gate 1 FAIL — the Alaska Public Media May 26 article (STAK AI data center) does not mention Quintillion fiber. Gate 3 FAIL — FCC DA-26-324 PDF is unreadable in binary form; FCC docket page returns 503; FCC cable landing license transfer application for GCI-Quintillion had not appeared in the IBFS database as of scouting. C_F2/C_CS1 (NANA Regional Broadband Network): Gate 1 FAIL — news trigger is an April 16, 2026 government press release (52 days outside broadened window, not an independent news outlet). Gate 3 FAIL — NANA board page returns 403; NANA Drake acquisition page returns 403; USACE poa.usace.army.mil returns 403. L3, L4, and L5 controlling actors cannot be verified. C_F3 (GCI-Quintillion Consolidation): Gate 1 FAIL, trigger outside any window. C_V2 (CMS Rural Health RHTP): Gate 1 FAIL, agency page not independent outlet, confirmed in prior run. C_V3 (GSA OASIS+ ANC 8(a) On-Ramp): Gate 5 FAIL (PCO unnamed); Gate 7 risk (SBA 8(a) recent repeat). C_CS3 (BSNC NHO Portfolio): Gate 7 FAIL (same SBA 8(a) layer chain as May 25, 2026 anatomy). C_R2 (DAF Enhanced Use Lease): Gate 1 FAIL, ADN May 5 trigger is outside broadened window, confirmed failure across multiple prior runs. C_R3 (USACE NWP 39/Section 404 STAK): Gate 5 FAIL (USACE Alaska District Commander not publicly named, poa.usace.army.mil returns 403); Gate 7 risk (STAK project already anatomized May 30). No mechanism survived both the 14-day and 21-day windows with all seven gates intact.

Dropped Mechanisms (11 candidates, all 4 categories)

  • Alaska BEAD Broadband Grant Program — Subgrant Execution Stack [vehicles]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie|missing_primary_source_per_layer
    Gate 1: In-window articles (KUCB May 27, Alaska Public Media June 1) cover GCI Aleutian cable outage and satellite backup; neither mentions BEAD, Alaska Broadband Office, Thomas Lochner, or subgrantee grant agreements — connection is inferential, not direct. Gate 3: Layer 2 (NIST grants officer) unnamed in all fetchable sources; Thomas Lochner appears only via an email address in an image-heavy PDF, not a named-role primary source; Layer 5 (THPO veto) not documented in any fetchable agency page.
  • Doyon Limited NTIA Tribal Broadband Grant CEO Transition Stack [capital_sovereignty]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie|diffuse_chokepoint
    Gate 1: Doyon CEO announcement was published March 9, 2026 — outside the broadened 21-day window. Source is a corporate newsroom, not an independent news outlet. No independent news outlet covered the CEO transition or fiber project in the May 17–June 7 window. Gate 5: Winkelman's binary individual authority (vs. Doyon board) to authorize July 2026 cable-laying is not documented in any fetchable primary source.
  • NRC Part 57 Microreactor Licensing Stack [regulatory]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie|missing_primary_source_per_layer|diffuse_chokepoint
    Gate 1: Primary trigger (POWER Magazine April 27, 2026) is 41 days before June 7, outside both 14-day and 21-day windows. June 5 Antares criticality article is in-window but does not mention Alaska, Eielson AFB, or NRC Part 57. Gate 3: Orrick LLP L2 URL returns 404; NRC OAR agency page returns 404; DEC siting permit page does not name a controlling official. Gate 5: Alaska DEC Layer does not name a specific siting permit decision-maker.
  • Quintillion Nome-to-Homer Express Arctic Cable Authorization Stack [facilities]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie|missing_primary_source_per_layer
    Gate 1: Alaska Public Media May 26 article (STAK AI data center) does not mention Quintillion fiber; GCI acquisition trigger is April 22, outside window. Gate 3: FCC DA-26-324 PDF unreadable in binary; FCC docket page returns 503; FCC cable landing license transfer application had not appeared in IBFS database as of scouting.
  • NANA Regional Broadband Network Multi-Layer Stack [facilities]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie|missing_primary_source_per_layer
    Gate 1: FPISC press release (April 16, 2026) is 52 days outside the broadened window AND is a government press release, not an independent news outlet. Gate 3: NANA board page returns 403; NANA Drake acquisition page returns 403; USACE poa.usace.army.mil returns 403. L3, L4, L5 controlling actors cannot be verified.
  • GCI-Quintillion Arctic Fiber Consolidation Regulatory Approval Stack [facilities]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie
    GCI announcement April 22 and Q1 8-K May 7 are both outside the 14-day window and 21-day broadened window. No post-May-17 independent news article about the acquisition regulatory review was confirmed.
  • Alaska CMS Rural Health Transformation Program — Subgrant Disbursement Stack [vehicles]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie
    Gate 1: The June 1 trigger is an agency website page (health.alaska.gov), not an independent news outlet. Identical failure reason as the 2026-06-07 first run.
  • GSA OASIS+ Phase II — ANC 8(a) On-Ramp [vehicles]
    Drop reason: diffuse_chokepoint|recent_repeat_risk
    Gate 5: The specific PCO who issues Notice to Proceed is unnamed in any primary source; Gruenbaum (FAS Commissioner) is not the binary decision-maker at the contract award layer. Gate 7 risk: SBA 8(a) program compliance review shares layer chain of the May 25, 2026 ANC 8(a) anatomy.
  • BSNC NHO Portfolio Acquisition Capital Stack [capital_sovereignty]
    Drop reason: recent_repeat
    Gate 7 FAIL: The SBA 8(a) program compliance review chokepoint is the same layer chain as the ANC 8(a) Sole-Source Federal Contracting Pipeline anatomized May 25, 2026.
  • DAF Alaska Enhanced Use Lease [regulatory]
    Drop reason: no_news_tie
    Gate 1 FAIL: ADN May 5, 2026 trigger is outside the 14-day and 21-day windows. Has failed Gate 1 in every prior run since May 3.
  • USACE NWP 39 / Section 404 for STAK North Slope [regulatory]
    Drop reason: diffuse_chokepoint|recent_repeat_risk
    Gate 5 FAIL: USACE Alaska District Commander not publicly named; poa.usace.army.mil returns 403. Gate 7 risk: STAK North Slope project already anatomized May 30, 2026.

Editor's Note

Second run on 2026-06-07 (branch suffix -02). The first run today (claude/linkedin-stack-2026-06-07) selected the BLM NPR-A Rulemaking Stack. This second run was a full fresh pass across all four mechanism categories.

Discovery: 4 scouts ran in parallel across facilities, vehicles, capital_sovereignty, and regulatory categories. 12 candidate mechanisms were surfaced.

Gating: The stack-mapper applied the seven-point anti-confabulation gate to all 12 candidates. Zero survived the 14-day window (May 24–June 7). The window was broadened to 21 days (May 17–June 7) per protocol. Zero survived the broadened window.

This is the second consecutive no-target second run today. The most promising candidates were the BEAD Subgrant Execution Stack (strong named actor — Thomas Lochner — but in-window articles on the GCI Aleutian cable break didn't directly mention BEAD or the ABO, making the Gate 1 connection inferential) and the NRC Part 57 Microreactor Licensing Stack (excellent mechanism depth, clear single-actor chokepoint in Jeremy Bowen — but the primary news trigger predates both windows by 41 days).

Mechanisms to watch next cycle:
- Alaska BEAD Subgrant Execution (Thomas Lochner, ABO Director) — if any independent outlet covers the grant agreement execution process directly, this passes Gate 1 cleanly
- NRC Part 57 / Oklo microreactor Alaska path — check for any in-window news story citing Alaska, Eielson, or Oklo in connection with Part 57 comment period (closes June 15)
- Doyon CEO transition (Dan Winkelman, effective June 1) + July fiber cable-laying decision — needs an independent outlet story and board vs. CEO authority clarification
- GCI-Quintillion FCC IBFS transfer-of-control filing — once filed in the IBFS database, this becomes a strong candidate with clear primary-source layer chain

No image render. No score report. Email always ships — this is the correct outcome when no mechanism can clear the anti-confabulation gate.
